newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: TAP could close due pilots' strike-paper.
newsitem.headline: TAP could close due pilots' strike-paper.

text.p: The Portuguese government believes that a planned pilots' strike threatens the financial viability of state airline TAP-Air Portugal and could force it to close, a Lisbon newspaper reported on Friday.

Diario Economico newspaper quoted a government document, made available to the newspaper, as saying: "This strike could jeopardise definitively the financial viability of the company and lead to its closure."

The document of the office of the Under-Secretary for Transport added: "The government forecasts that the company will suffer a financial rupture in November, and expects difficulty in paying salaries to all (TAP) workers (in that month)."
Portugal's main pilots' union has told TAP that it plans an indefinite strike over working hours from Monday.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment on the newspaper report.
In April TAP pilots staged a two-day stoppage over working hours which grounded international flights and left around 14,000 passengers stranded.
TAP posted a 10.5 billion escudo ($56.6 million) net loss for 1996 but its chairman last April forecast a return to profit this year and in 1998.
